Convex interpolation of three sampled majorant values is possible exactly under the floor and midpoint Jensen conditions. Reducing the middle value to b and the endpoint sum to 2b improves the objective. On the balanced two-active branch the endpoint cost improves toward b, and on the one-active branch the endpoint cost improves toward a. The zero branch and clipping equalities are accounted for. The two attaining majorants are actual affine functions.

If a^q≤cb^q the balanced endpoint contributions and the far-end contribution vanish, giving γ(b^q+a^q)<γM. Binary product slices independently obey the same upper bound and the original affine optimizer extended constantly in the extra coordinates attains the exact product value.

For q=1 the ratio has derivative numerators −1 and 6 in the two ranges of a/b, giving the unique minimum 5/7 at 2/3. Independently checked M=7, J*=5/2 at all three exhibited optimizing majorants, J*/2=5/4, and the formal B=3/2 inequalities.

Central symmetry of the original mixed measure and the exact continuous-coordinate half cut give maximum normalized depth 1/2. Any actual cap cover must cover the origin, so its maximum mass is at least 7/2. Adding positive weights to scalar majorant inequalities yields an average of right sides bounded by J*.
